text.description: Follow the trail past Post Corral Creek to Fleming and Lower Indian lakes, then go cross-country up grassy slopes to the west ridge and along it to the top. About 2 miles and 2,000 ft past the lake.

Follow Tombstone Creek to Tombstone Pass, traverse to the cirque below the summit and climb the southwest ridge to the summit block. The block itself is a short 5.4 crack on the south side. Class 2 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

text.description: Hike the Mono Creek trail to Mott Lake, go cross-country to Bighorn Lake, and climb the mostly solid east face. Descend the sandy south face.
Class 3 to the summit block, which is Class 4.

text.description: Follow the Meysan Lake trail, then climb talus to a chute that leads to the plateau and summit. Snow or ice can choke the chute well into summer.
A well-defined trail climbs through forest and Cold Stream Meadow toward the south ridge and summit. Easy and non-technical.

text.description: Hike the Meysan Lakes trail to the lake, then climb the loose gully near the south side of the east ridge to the plateau and the summit blocks. Scree and talus all the way.

Reach Arc Pass, then climb scree and talus to the south summit. Downclimb a class 3 step into the notch, go up a short way and follow a ramp left onto easy scrambling to the highest point. Exposed; a rope may be welcome.

text.description: The easy side is the southwest slope above the Crabtree Lakes. A common long approach crosses Discovery Pass and Crabtree Pass; the ridge from Crabtree Pass is slower and reaches class 3.
A straightforward class 2 line starts just south of the summit and angles up the west face to a broad gully.

text.description: Climb the loose talus chute out of Armstrong Canyon to the crest, cross the high basin, and follow the talus of the east ridge to the summit. Water is scarce and the chute is loose.

text.description: Hike over Kearsarge Pass to the Bullfrog Lake area, then climb the loose scree and talus slopes to the summit ridge. The last few hundred feet are steeper, with a few easy moves on dark rock near the top.

text.description: Hike over Taboose Pass and cross the Kings River, then go cross-country to the base of the east ridge. Climb the blocky toe and scramble the ridge, which has exposed class 3 with a move or two harder.

text.description: Hike the trail around Florence Lake and across the San Joaquin, take the cutoff use trail toward Selden Pass, and climb to Sallie Keyes Lakes. Continue over boulders and a bench below the summit; the final slopes are easier than they look.
Follow the Twin Lakes trail to Silliman Creek, go up the creek to Silliman Meadow and the friction slabs to Silliman Lake. Continue to the upper lake and climb the south slope to the summit.
